blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
. The presence of lens flares in images can significantly reduce the quality of downstream application results for tasks such as 3D scene reconstruction. This is because lens flares are a property of the camera imaging system, and not a part of the underlying scene being modeled. There are previous methods that tackle the removal of small flares focused around a light source. However, existing methods struggle with large flares, such as those that fill the entire image. In this work, we compile a novel dataset for large-flare removal, combining publicly available real-world data with a procedural generation pipeline. We fine-tune a diffusion-based model on our dataset to remove complex, large lens flares.
On the other hand, lens flares remain effective artistic tools, widely used in the media. While there are ways to simulate 2D flares, representing and reconstructing lens flares consistently across multiple views has not yet been explored. To achieve this, we introduce a flare representation model that leverages the symmetry of lens flares about the camera’s principal point. We propose a computational pipeline to jointly optimize this flare model and a Gaussian splatting model (3DGS). This enables the decomposition of a 3D scene into lens flares and the scene itself, using our flare-removal model. Because the reconstructed flare is explicit and re-renderable, it can be edited and transferred to novel images and new 3D scenes. We evaluate removal on an established benchmark and a new one for large reflective flares, quantify the flare/scene decomposition directly, and show that the pipeline is robust to errors in automatic light-source localization.

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 导言

blocks.en: Lens flares are artifacts caused by unintended light paths passing through the lens when a camera observes a sufficiently bright light source in the scene. In this work, we will refer to two subjective categories of lens flare appearance, see Fig. 2 . Scattering flares occur due to dust, lens defects, and scratches on lenses, causing lens glares, shimmer, and streaks in images, respectively. Reflective flares occur due to lens ensembles where lenses reflect a small percentage of the incident light.

blocks.en: 1.1. Lens flare removal
blocks.zh: 1.1. 抛光灯

blocks.en: In many downstream applications, it is important to remove lens flares. Existing flare removal methods ( Dai et al., 2023a ; Wu et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) use real and synthetic lens flare datasets to add synthetic flares to images from a dataset without flares and learn to predict the original flare-free images. Such datasets are mainly composed of scattering flares. Although one dataset contains a few reflective flares, they cover a relatively small area and are not full-frame reflective flares. To augment these datasets, we compile a novel dataset with real-world large reflective flares and augment it with procedurally generated flares. As baselines, we train previously proposed models on our dataset for flare removal. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach that demonstrates that fine-tuning a diffusion model with LoRA for flare removal on these datasets yields better results, which also lead to better multi-view 3D reconstructions (Sec. 5.2 ). We evaluate all of the models on the scattering-flare-removal benchmark from Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) and propose a new benchmark for large reflective-flare removal. Further, we compile a dataset of 5 5 flare corrupted scenes to evaluate the performance of the flare-removal models across multiple views. We demonstrate that, on each benchmark, one of our two models outperforms all prior methods.

blocks.en: 1.2. Lens flare representation and reconstruction
blocks.zh: 1.2. 闪光灯代表和重建

blocks.en: Lens flares are an important artistic tool in film, games, and virtual production, where they add cinematic realism and convey the presence of bright light sources. For downstream reconstruction tasks, although they are undesirable, understanding their effects and synthesizing them would help us better control the 3D reconstruction as lens flares are unavoidable in many situations. Existing flare simulators – stock compositing, procedural, and physically-based (Tab. 1 ) – can synthesize plausible flares, but none reconstruct the actual pattern of a given capture: physically-based methods only achieve viewpoint-correct appearance when the lens prescription is precisely known, diffractive effects, among the most distinctive aspects of lens flares, are computationally intractable to simulate at macroscopic lens scales, and modeling every possible real-world light source is not scalable. Our goal is instead to reconstruct the actual flare patterns present in captured footage, preserving lens- and capture-specific characteristics. For instance, in Fig. 3 , we see that the same lens leads to different types of lens flares with different light sources. Further, realistically editing lens flares into images requires extensive manual artistic effort. A view-consistent 3D flare representation is therefore valuable beyond removal: it enables reconstruction, and transfer of captured flares onto novel target images (see Fig. 1 ) and onto novel target scenes (see Fig. 14 ), none of which a per-image 2D removal model can provide.
blocks.zh: 列恩斯耀斑是电影,游戏,以及虚拟制作中的重要艺术工具,它们在这里加入了电影现实主义,传达了亮光源的存在. 对于下游的重建任务,尽管它们不可取,但了解其影响和加以综合将有助于我们更好地控制三维重建,因为在许多情况下,透镜照明物是不可避免的。 现有的耀斑模拟器 — — 库存堆肥、程序性和基于物理的(Tab. 1) — — 可以合成假想的耀斑,但没有人能重建一个特定捕捉的实际模式:只有精确知道镜头处方时,以物理为基础的方法才能实现对角度的正确外观,在镜头耀斑最显著的方面中,偏振效应在计算上是难以在宏观镜头尺度上模拟的,而模拟每一个可能的现实世界光源是无法伸缩的。 相反,我们的目标是重建所拍摄到的镜头中的实际耀斑图案,保留镜头和捕捉特性。 例如,在图3中,我们看到相同的镜头会导致不同光源的不同类型的镜头耀斑. 此外,现实地将镜头照明弹编辑成图像需要大量人工艺术努力。 因此,与视野一致的3D照明弹表示值超出清除值:它可以使被捕获的照明弹能够重建,并转移到新的目标图像(见图1)和新的目标场景(见图14)上,而每个图像的2D清除模型都无法提供。

blocks.en: Our goal is to enable reconstruction and real-time rendering of flares from any viewpoint. Reconstructing lens flares is inherently different from reconstructing a 3D scene, for instance, using Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). In 3DGS, we assume that we can capture a static 3D scene from different viewpoints. However, this does not hold for lens flares, which are not part of the 3D scene and change with the relative motion between the light sources and the camera, i.e., they are 3D inconsistent. Even deformable 3DGS methods assume that the underlying motion is 3D consistent and fail to reconstruct reflective lens flares. Hence, when we reconstruct a scene with images containing lens flares using 3DGS, the models either bake them into the 3D scene or ignore them altogether, as shown in Fig. 4 .
blocks.zh: 我们的目标是使重建和从任何角度实时发射照明弹成为可能。 重建镜头照明弹本质上不同于重建一个3D场景,例如使用高斯电镀(3DGS). 在3DGS中,我们假设我们可以从不同的角度捕捉一个静态的3D场景. 然而,这对镜头信号弹来说并不重要,这些信号弹不属于3D场景的一部分,随着光源和相机之间的相对运动而变化,即它们是3D不一致的. 甚至可变形的3DGS方法也假设基础运动是3D一致的,无法重建反射镜头耀斑. 因此,当我们用3DGS 来重建一个包含镜头信号弹的场景时,模型要么将其烤入3D场景中,要么完全忽略,如Fig所示. 4 (英语).

blocks.en: Therefore, we need a novel 3D representation that can reproduce the changing lens flare across different views. To achieve this, we model lens flares using Gaussians that are anchored to the camera on a near-plane in front of the scene, rather than as free-floating geometry in world space; this reflects the fact that flares are produced by the imaging system itself and move with the camera. Further, we design the flare representation model per light source based on the fact that lens flares approximately lie along the line joining the light source and the principal point in 2D ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) . We constrain, by design, that all Gaussians lie on the projected 2D line connecting each light source to the camera’s principal point. We learn a deformation field to move and modulate lens flares based on the light and camera locations. We position the plane right after the near plane and rasterize it together with the scene in a single pass, so the flare adds little to rasterization cost and the full model still renders in real time. This makes captured flares directly usable in interactive settings such as games and VR/AR, where view-consistent camera effects are needed to blend virtual content convincingly with real footage. Our representation is consistent with 3DGS rasterizers and can be ported to any of its variants.
blocks.zh: 因此,我们需要一个新的3D代表 可以复制 变化的镜头耀斑 不同的观点。 为了实现这一点,我们用在现场前的近平面上锚定在相机上的高斯人来模拟镜头照明弹,而不是作为世界空间中自由浮动的几何;这反映了信号弹是由成像系统本身产生的,并随相机一起移动的事实. 此外,我们设计每个光源的耀斑表示模型所依据的事实是,镜头耀斑大约位于连接光源的线上,主要点在2D(Koreban and Schechner,2009年;Dai等人,2023年b)。 我们通过设计来限制所有高斯人 都停留在将每个光源连接到相机主要点的2D线上。 我们学习一个变形场,根据光线和相机位置移动和调制镜头照明弹. 我们把飞机定位在接近的飞机后, 把它和场景一起用一个通道, 所以照明弹很少增加光栅化成本, 整个模型仍然实时产生。 这使得俘获的耀斑可以直接用于游戏和VR/AR等互动环境中,在这种环境中,需要符合视图的相机效果才能令人信服地将虚拟内容与真实的镜头混合. 我们的表示与3DGS光栅机一致,可以移植到其任何变体上.

blocks.en: Moreover, we collect a dataset of 9 9 diverse scenes with reflective flares from multiple views to demonstrate that our lens flare model can be trained alongside 3DGS to automatically decompose a set of images into flares and scene. To better control decomposition, we supervise the 3DGS model using our removal model, enabling clean 3DGS reconstruction and lens-flare reconstruction across multiple views.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们收集了9个不同场景的数据集,这些场景从多个角度反射耀斑,以表明我们的镜头耀斑模型可以和3DGS一起训练,将一组图像自动分解成耀斑和场景. 为了更好地控制分解,我们使用我们的去除模型来监督3DGS模型,使得清洁的3DGS重建以及透镜光板重建跨越多个视角.

blocks.en: Our contributions can be summarized as follows, • a flare representation model for 3D scenes using Gaussian splatting, • a flare removal model obtained by fine-tuning a pretrained diffusion model with real-world scattering flares and our novel dataset of large, real-world reflective flares • a pipeline for decomposed reconstruction of a set of multi-view images into scene Gaussians, and flare Gaussians • applications enabled by our flare representation, including editing and transfer of a captured flare onto novel images and 3D scenes

blocks.en: In this section, we discuss works most relevant to our paper. We discuss existing methods for removing flares, followed by methods for 3D reconstruction.

blocks.en: Figure 5. Our lens flare removal model (middle). We fine-tune the diffusion model from Difix3D+ ( Wu et al., 2025 ) with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) , enabling one-step flare removal. We train two models, Ours and Ours-wGlare, without lens glare and with lens glare, respectively, as shown above (right, target supervision). We note that while the model with light glare might be subjectively preferred by an end user, the one without light glare is more realistic. To train our models, we add a flare image from our flare datasets to an image from the training dataset, yielding a corrupted input, and train them using the loss from  Eq. ( 2 ). A diagram of the lens flare removal pipeline. On the left, two example inputs are formed by adding a flare image (a starburst light) to a clean image (a lake at dusk, or a tree against the sky) in linear space, producing a flare-corrupted image. blocks.en: 2.1. Flare Removal
blocks.zh: 2.1. 消除火焰

blocks.en:
FR ( Wu et al., 2021 ) is the pioneering work to train a UNet ( Ronneberger et al., 2015 ) to remove lens flares. Synthetic flares are added to a dataset of images, and the model is supervised with the flare-free images. Light sources are added to the generated flare-free images through threshold-based light detection. Later, many methods updated the model to UFormer ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , which remains the best performer across many datasets. Flare7K ( Dai et al., 2022 ) introduced a synthetic dataset composed of scattering and reflective flares, which helped improve the flare removal models greatly. Building on this method, Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) introduced a real scattering flares dataset, which further improved flare removal models. Along with the dataset, it also proposed a real-world benchmark for flare removal. However, this benchmark only tests for scattering flares and ignores lens glares, discussed later in the experiments section. BracketFlare ( Dai et al., 2023b ) is trained to remove a single small reflective flare that is symmetric around the principal point of the camera using synthetic data generation based on images captured using different exposures. On the other hand, DiffFlare ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) learns to guide a pretrained multi-step latent diffusion model for scattering flare removal. ACL-FR ( Zhou et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) employs adversarial curve learning to model the image signal processing pipeline, thereby achieving improved flare removal for various camera types and enhanced preservation of lighting characteristics. FlareX ( Lishen et al., 2025 ) proposes a novel synthetic dataset for flare removal, including some large flares, which might benefit our model. LightsOut ( Tsai et al., 2025 ) proposes to outpaint an image to generate light sources for removing off-screen lens flares. Deng et al. ( Deng et al., 2024 ) estimate a flare-level map to guide blind flare removal, and Deflare-Net ( Ghodesawar et al., 2023 ) couples flare detection with removal; neither releases code or models, so we do not compare against them quantitatively.
Contrary to existing methods, which focus on more exactly modeling the physics of flare corruption, we leverage a pretrained single-step diffusion model that enables fast flare removal by fine-tuning with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) on relatively small real data. Furthermore, we introduce a dataset of real full-image reflective flares and propose a reflective flare-removal benchmark that is not limited to nighttime flares.
blocks.zh:
FR(Wu et al., 2021年)是培训一台UNet(Ronneberger et al., 2015年)去除镜头照明弹的开创性工作. 合成耀斑被添加到图像的数据集中,模型与无耀斑的图像一起监督. 光源通过阈值光探测加入生成的无耀斑图像. 后来,许多方法将该模型更新到UFormer(Wang等人,2022年),这仍然是许多数据集中表现最好的. Flare7K(Dai等人,2022年)引入了由散射和反射耀斑组成的合成数据集,这极大地改善了耀斑清除模型. 基于这种方法, Flare7K++ (Dai等人,2023a)引入了真正的散射耀斑数据集,这进一步改善了耀斑清除模型. 除了数据集外,它还提出了消除耀斑的现实世界基准。 然而,这个基准仅用于对散射耀斑的测试,而忽略了实验部分后面讨论的镜头光泽. BracketFlare(Dai等人,2023年b)经过培训,可以使用基于通过不同曝光捕获的图像的合成数据生成,去除相机主点周围对称的单一小反射耀斑. 另一方面,DiffFlare(Zhou等人,2024年)学习指导一种经过预先训练的多步骤潜在扩散模型,用于分散耀斑清除. ACL-FR(Zhou等人,2023年;Zhou等人,2025年)采用对抗曲线学习来模拟图像信号处理管道,从而改进了各种相机类型的耀斑清除,加强了照明特性的保存. 火焰X (Lishen等人,2025年)提出了用于清除耀斑的新型合成数据集,包括一些大型耀斑,这可能对我们的模式有利. 灯光 出局(Tsai等人,2025年)提议将图像涂成外层,以产生光源,去除屏幕外的镜头照明弹. 邓等. (Deng等人, 2024年)估算出用于引导盲光弹清除的耀斑水平图,以及Deflare-Net(Ghodesawar等人, 2023年)夫妇耀斑探测和清除;无论是释放代码还是模型,我们都没有在数量上加以比较.
与注重更精确地模拟耀斑腐败物理的现有方法相反,我们利用预先训练的单步扩散模型,通过微调LORA(Hu等人,2022年)在相对小的真实数据上迅速清除耀斑。 此外,我们采用了一套真实的全影像反射照明弹的数据集,并提出了不仅限于夜间照明弹的反射照明弹清除基准。

blocks.en: 2.1.1. Flare removal in 3D Reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 2.1.1. 运输 3D重建中的火焰清除.

blocks.en: GN-FR ( Matta et al., 2024 ) is designed to remove small scattering flares from 3D scenes using a predicted flare mask. The idea is to completely ignore the regions with flares during the supervision of a generalizable NeRF 3D reconstruction model. Note that their data and code are not publicly released . The idea is built similarly to robust novel view synthesis methods ( Sabour et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2023 ) , where distractors are detected and ignored. However, when the input contains large scattering or reflective flares, most of the information from these images is lost. We demonstrate the strength of our flare removal model in that it consistently removes flares across multi-view images without losing scene information. We also propose a novel benchmark for evaluating 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis under the presence of challenging scattering flares.
blocks.zh: GN-FR(Matta等人,2024年)旨在利用预测的耀斑罩去除3D场景中的小散射耀斑. 想法是在监督通用的NERF 3D重建模型时,完全忽略带有耀斑的区域. 请注意,他们的数据和代码没有公开发布。 这个想法与强壮的新颖观点合成方法类似(Sabour等人,2025年;Zhu等人,2023年),其中分辨器被检测和忽略. 然而,当输入含有大量散射或反射耀斑时,这些图像的大部分信息就会丢失. 我们证明了我们的耀斑清除模型的优点,因为它在不丢失场景信息的情况下,不断在多景图像中清除耀斑。 我们还提出一个新的基准,用于评估3D重建以及在具有挑战性的散射信号弹存在下的新观点综合。

blocks.en: 2.2. Lens Flare Representation
blocks.zh: 2.2. 灯光代表

blocks.en: 2.2.1. Physically-based Lens Flare Representations.
blocks.zh: 2.2.1. 以身体为主的Lens火焰代表。

blocks.en: Most existing methods ( Hullin et al., 2011 ; Maurer, 2024 ; Bodonyi and Kunkli, 2023 ; Bodonyi et al., 2025 ; Lee and Eisemann, 2013 ) model characteristics of specific lens ensembles for producing lens flares and focus on enabling real-time rendering of the modeled lens flares. Closer to our work, Koreban and Schechner ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ) analyze the geometric structure of aperture-ghost flares and show that, under lens rotational symmetry, ghost positions lie on the line connecting the light source projection and the optical center in the image plane. We exploit this same geometric property as a constraint inside a differentiable 3DGS pipeline.
blocks.zh: 大多数现有方法(Hullin等人,2011年;Maurer,2024年;Bodonyi和Kunkli,2023年;Bodonyi等人,2025年;Lee和Eisemann,2013年)是生产镜头耀斑的特定镜头组合的模型特性,并侧重于能够实时渲染模型镜头耀斑. 更接近于我们的工作,科雷班和舍克纳(科雷班和舍克纳,2009年)分析了孔径-鬼信号弹的几何结构,并显示在镜头旋转对称下,幽灵位置位于连接光源投影和图像平面光学中心的线上. 我们利用同样的几何属性 来限制不同的3DGS管道

blocks.en: 2.2.2. 3D Lens Flare Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 2.2.2. 3D 灯光重建

blocks.en: Flare representation is a hard task, as lens flares, in general, are not 3D consistent. Therefore, existing 3D Gaussian splatting ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) and even deformable 3DGS ( Luiten et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) reconstruction methods fail to represent lens flares, see Fig. 4 . However, it can be seen that scattering lens flares closer to the light source (in images) do not change significantly across views and are reconstructed near the light source in a 3D scene, even though they are not 3D-consistent. Yet, the models ignore reflective flares completely in the reconstructions and are heavily affected by scattering flares, as shown in Fig. 12 . Our proposed reconstruction pipeline, based on our flare representation model, decomposes and represents different kinds of lens flares.
blocks.zh: 火焰表示是一项艰巨的任务,因为镜头信号弹一般来说并不3D一致. 因此,现有的3D高斯电镀(Kerbl等人,2023年)甚至可变形的3DGS(Luiten等人,2024年;Yang等人,2023年;Wu等人,2024年)重建方法未能代表透镜照明弹,见Fig. 4. 然而,可以看到,离光源更近的散射镜头耀斑(在图像中)在视界之间没有显著变化,并在3D场景中重建在光源附近,尽管它们并非3D一致. 然而,如图12所示,这些模型完全无视重建过程中的反射照明弹,并受到散射照明弹的严重影响。 我们提议的重建管道,基于我们的耀斑表示模型,会分解并代表不同种类的透镜照明弹.

blocks.en: 3. Method
blocks.zh: 3个 方法

blocks.en: In this work, we aim to develop a lens flare removal model and use it to learn a 3D representation of lens flares. We fine-tune a latent diffusion model as our flare removal model. We elaborate on it in the first part of this section.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们的目标是开发一个镜头照明弹清除模型,并利用它来学习透镜照明弹的3D表示. 我们微调一个潜在的扩散模型 作为我们的耀斑清除模型。 我们将在本节第一部分阐述这个问题。

blocks.en: To represent lens flares in 3D, we adopt a dynamic Gaussian splatting model, treating them as 3D Gaussians moving on a 2D plane. While rendering the scene, we place this 2D plane in front of the scene 3DGS and render the scene and the flares together.
blocks.zh: 为了在3D中代表透镜耀斑,我们采用了动态高斯电镀模型,把它们当作在2D平面上移动的3D高斯人. 在制作场景的同时,我们把这架2D飞机放在场景3DGS前面,使场景和照明弹合在一起.

blocks.en: 3.1. Lens Flare Removal
blocks.zh: 3.1. 升降灯

blocks.en: Lens flares are primarily caused by unintended light paths passing through a lens when a camera observes a sufficiently bright light source. They are undesirable in many cases. Given the intractability of modeling the effects of different light sources on various lens types, we need a learning-based solution for lens flare removal. Most existing lens-flare removal models exclusively focus on scattering flares, small reflective flares, and shimmer.
blocks.zh: 镜头耀斑主要是在镜头观测到足够亮的光源时意外通过透镜的光路造成的. 它们在许多情况下是不可取的。 鉴于不同光源在各种镜头类型上的效果的建模是不可磨灭的,我们需要一个基于学习的镜头耀斑清除解决方案. 现有的大多数透镜光板清除模型都专门侧重于散射耀斑、小反射耀斑和闪光。

blocks.en: 3.1.2. Diffusion-based removal model
blocks.zh: 3.1.2. 基于扩散的清除模式

blocks.en: We introduce a unified flare removal model that works with different types of lens flares - scattering, and reflective (both full image and small). We fine-tune a latent diffusion model for this task. Specifically, we adopt the diffusion model in Difix3D+ ( Wu et al., 2025 ) . The model is trained on a dataset of billions of images, making it well-suited for generating flare-free images. Furthermore, the fine-tuning paradigm in Difix3D+, based on single-step image-to-image translation models, is ideally suited to our task.

blocks.en: 3.1.3. Training data
blocks.zh: 3.1.3. 培训数据

blocks.en: Obtaining real-world paired data for flare removal is challenging, as it requires two identical cameras at the exact same locations: one capturing an image with flares and one without. Therefore, similar to baselines ( Dai et al., 2023a ; Wu et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) , we obtain paired data by adding flare images from our lens flare datasets (both synthetic and real) to an image dataset, Flickr24K ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) in the linear space. Further, we add the expected light source from the dataset to the supervision image, I g = ( I i ​ m ​ a ​ g ​ e γ + I l ​ i ​ g ​ h ​ t γ ) 1 / γ I_{g}=(I_{image}^{\gamma}+I_{light}^{\gamma})^{1/\gamma} . blocks.en: 3.2. Lens Flare Representation and Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 3.2. 伦斯火焰代表和重建

blocks.en:
Representing lens flares using physically based models across different lens types is challenging, as different lens ensembles produce distinct flares under varying light sources, necessitating accurate physical models of those sources in real-world scenes. Further, accurately modeling the effect of the lenses requires not only precise prescriptions for all lens elements but also modeling of coherent propagation effects at the wavelength scale to precisely reproduce lens flares, with corresponding geometric detail for all components in the lens, particularly parts like iris blades that produce diffraction.
Therefore, we adopt Gaussian splatting to represent and reconstruct lens flares in a given scene.
blocks.zh:
使用不同镜头类型的物理模型来表示镜头信号弹具有挑战性,因为不同的镜头组合在不同光源下产生不同的信号弹,因此需要在现实世界的场景中对这些来源进行准确的物理模型。 此外,精确地模拟镜头的效果不仅需要对所有镜头元素作出精确的处方,还需要在波长尺度上模拟一致的传播效果,以精确地复制镜头耀斑,对镜头中的所有组件,特别是产生疏松作用的虹膜叶片等部分进行相应的几何细节.
因此,我们采用高斯滑板来代表和重建特定场景中的镜头照明弹.

blocks.en: To achieve this, we model lens flares as 3D Gaussians on a plane in front of the near plane, and move them based on the camera location. We render the scene together with the Gaussians. Furthermore, we model the Gaussians representing flares as lying on a line between the image’s principal point and the light source’s position in the image. We illustrate this in  Fig. 6 . The flare model is jointly optimized along with a Gaussian splatting ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) model representing the scene.

blocks.zh: 3.2.1. 高斯滑板

blocks.en:
Our goal is to represent lens flares with minimum overhead over the scene representation - 3DGS. Therefore, we use 3D Gaussians as the final output of our lens flare representation, allowing us to rasterize the scene along with the lens flare effects.
In 3DGS ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) , the scene is modeled as a collection of 3D Gaussians 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , endowed with a mean μ \mu , scale s s , covariance Σ \Sigma , opacity σ \sigma , and color as spherical harmonics with b b -bases s ​ h sh ; 𝒢 = { μ , s , Σ , σ , s ​ h } \mathcal{G}=\{\mu,s,\Sigma,\sigma,sh\} . The Gaussians are initialized with a point cloud from Colmap ( Schönberger et al., 2016 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ) . The Gaussians are rasterized to input camera locations, and the parameters are optimized using a loss function that compares the input images with the rasterized images. We refer the readers to 3DGS ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) for a more elaborate explanation.

blocks.en: Our representation places flares on the image-plane line through the principal point p p and the projected light location l l ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) , and parameterizes each flare component by its radial position along that line. Concretely, each flare component is a set of canonical 1D Gaussians whose scalar mean μ ∈ ℝ \mu\in\mathbb{R} encodes radial offset. A small MLP, conditioned on the camera and light positions, deforms these canonical Gaussians; the deformed scalar mean μ ′ \mu^{\prime} is then (i) lifted to a 2D image point via μ ′ ​ ( ( l + δ l ) − p ) + p \mu^{\prime}\big((l+\delta_{l})-p\big)+p , (ii) unprojected to a depth equal to the near plane + ϵ +\epsilon in the camera frame, and (iii) emitted as a standard 3DGS primitive (Fig. 7 ). Because the entire construction lives in the camera frame and produces standard 3DGS primitives, the scene rasterizer is reused unchanged, and the flare component is rigidly tied to the camera, independent of the scene geometry behind it. The remainder of this section details the parameterization, deformation MLP, and light-position correction.

blocks.en: Our lens flare model is inspired by the Deformable 3DGS ( Yang et al., 2023 ) (Def-3DGS). Our model features a set of canonical Gaussians representing lens flares, along with a deformation model that deforms them based on the light location and camera position. Unlike in Def-3DGS, however, the Gaussians in our lens flare model are one-dimensional ( μ ∈ ℝ 1 \mu\in\mathbb{R}^{1} , with a slight abuse of notation), as the location of the lens flares is generally restricted to the line connecting the principal point to the 2D position of the light source in image space ( Koreban and Schechner, 2009 ; Dai et al., 2023b ) . While Def-3DGS models condition on time, we condition our deformation model on the camera and light locations to modulate the canonical flare Gaussians, since lens flares depend on the relative positions of the camera and light.

blocks.en: 3.2.3. Light Positions
blocks.zh: 3.2.3. 轻便位置

blocks.en:
In an ideal lens-flare model, every Gaussian in the scene contributes to the lens flares and is attenuated proportionally to its intensity. However, even with reliable Gaussian intensities, instantiating the ideal flare model for every Gaussian in the scene – rather than for a small, sparse set of discrete emitters – is computationally wasteful. Further, an ideal camera sensor that captures the full dynamic range would make it
trivial to identify light sources directly from the Gaussians themselves, e.g., by
thresholding on intensity. But captured images have limited dynamic range, so the intensities recovered by a 3DGS reconstruction are an unreliable proxy for true radiance. Light sources are precisely the regions most prone to over-exposure and clipping.
blocks.zh:
在一个理想的镜头-荧光模型中,场景中的每一位高斯人都会对镜头耀斑作出贡献,并根据其强度按比例减弱. 然而,即使有可靠的高斯人密集度,对现场每一个高斯人 — — 而不是一小撮稀少的离散发射人 — — 的理想耀斑模型的即时化也是在计算上的浪费。 此外,一个理想的摄像传感器 能捕捉到整个动态范围
用来直接识别来自高斯人本身的光源的微不足道,例如:
强度的阈值。 但被捕获的图像的动态范围有限,因此3DGS重建恢复的强度是真光的不可靠的代称. 光源恰恰是最容易过度接触和剪切的区域。

blocks.en: Therefore, we approximate the flare contribution of the highest-intensity sources by estimating a discrete set of source centers (i.e., light sources). This means our model takes as input the number of light sources in the scene and their locations, which – not their intensities – drive the flare reconstruction (Sec. 3.2.2 ).

blocks.zh: 4.1 (中文(简体) ). 清除火焰

blocks.en: We train our flare removal model with the Flare7k++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) and the Flickr24K ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) datasets. However, the flare dataset is limited to small reflective flares. Therefore, we compile a large reflective flares dataset from publicly available real visual effects videos of large flares ( ActionVFX, 2026 ) . We obtain 1866 1866 training images from 90 90 clips spanning three effect categories (halo, icon and shimmer), and hold out 18 18 further clips entirely for testing, so that no test flare shares a source clip with any training flare. We compile the VFX benchmark by compositing flares from these held-out clips onto 128 128 images from our captures.

blocks.en: To quantify the differences between Flare7K++’s and our VFX flares, we measure, for each isolated flare layer, the fraction of the frame that contains 90 % 90\% of the flare’s energy, a threshold- and resolution-independent measure of spatial extent. Flare7K++’s reflective flares have a median coverage of 0.39 % 0.39\% (interquartile range (IQR) 0.13 0.13 – 1.81 % 1.81\% , N = 2000 N=2000 ), whereas the flares in our VFX dataset have a median of 78.0 % 78.0\% (IQR 69.1 69.1 – 82.5 % 82.5\% , N = 1866 N=1866 ); the IQRs do not overlap. Large full-frame reflective flares are therefore absent from existing data rather than merely under-represented. The two sets also differ in provenance. Flare7K++’s reflective flares are synthetic, generated from 10 10 base patterns; its real world subset, captured on the rear cameras of three smartphones, contains scattering flares only ( Dai et al., 2023a ) . Ours are real captures of large reflective flares. Lens diversity is therefore not a meaningful axis of comparison here. Synthetic flares have no associated lens, and the visual-effects footage does not publish one, so we characterize the two sets by flare extent instead.

blocks.en: Moreover, we identified that some lenses produce large, almost ring-shaped reflective lens flares that cover the entire image and are not captured by any of these datasets. Therefore, we procedurally create large circular flares with radially diminishing opacity towards the center. We achieve this by randomly sampling a center for the circle in the image and then a radius (a multiple of the minimum of the image’s height and width). We draw this circle, choosing a random color and opacity ( < 0.7 <0.7 ). Finally, we multiply the image by a radially increasing opacity mask, which is 0 0 at the center. Therefore, obtaining a ring-like flare. See Fig. 9 for examples.

blocks.zh: 4.1.1. 带有火焰的场景

blocks.en: Existing 3D scene datasets are carefully captured to not have any light sources. Therefore, we capture two datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of our flare removal model across multiple views and that of our flare representation model.
blocks.zh: 现有的3D场景数据集被仔细捕捉到没有任何光源. 因此,我们捕捉到两个数据集,以显示我们从多种观点出发的照明弹清除模型和我们的照明弹表示模型的有效性。

blocks.en: 4.1.2. Flare Removal from 3D Scenes
blocks.zh: 4.1.2. 从3D场景中清除火焰

blocks.en: We capture a set of 5 5 diverse indoor and outdoor scenes with different types of light sources and lens flares in the scenes. The scenes consist of 50 50 – 110 110 images, of which we reserve 10 % 10\% for testing. For a fair evaluation, we deliberately select test views that are flare-free, captured from positions where the light source falls outside the camera frustum or is sufficiently occluded; these views are held out of training and serve as unbiased scene-only ground truth for evaluating flare removal across multiple views, independent of any removal model’s output. See the supplement for examples of our test and training images.
blocks.zh: 我们捕捉到一套5个不同的室内和室外场景,场景中有不同类型的光源和镜头照明弹. 剧情由50 — 110幅影像组成, 其中我们保留10% — 10% — 用于测试。 为了进行公平的评价,我们故意选择没有照明弹的试验观点,从光源位于照相机门外的位置上捕获,或被充分占用;这些观点是未经训练而持有的,是评价从多种观点中清除照明弹的不带偏见的地面真理,独立于任何清除模型的输出。 我们的测试和训练图像的例子见补编。

blocks.en: 4.2. Flare Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 4.2. 火焰重建

blocks.en: We capture 9 9 diverse scenes spanning a mix of indoor and outdoor settings, multiple lens types (varying in focal length and ensemble), and a variety of real-world light sources – an LED headlamp, workshop lighting, a smartphone flashlight, a street lamp, and a purple-hued decorative light – so as to elicit a broad range of reflective flare patterns. We capture ∼ 1 \sim 1 min sequences, use 300 300 – 400 400 evenly spaced video frames for training, and 40 40 images from the remaining frames for testing. Held-out views far from the training trajectory are impractical here: we captured each sequence only for as long as the flare remained visible, so camera motion was bounded by the point at which the light left the frame and the flare vanished, rather than by any preference for a narrow sweep. These held-out frames are therefore interleaved with the training frames, so they test interpolation between nearby viewpoints within that range; extrapolation to new viewpoints and scenes is shown through transfer (Sec. 5.4 ) and in the supplementary webpage. Unlike ordinary scene content, flare appearance is governed by the light’s position relative to the optical axis rather than by scene-point parallax, and this mapping is highly nonlinear: small camera or light motions can produce disproportionately large changes in ghost position, halo extent, and streak orientation (Sec. 5.5 ). Interpolating this deformation between nearby frames is therefore non-trivial. Unlike the 5 5 -scene removal dataset above, a per-pixel ground-truth flare-free image and flare layer are intractable to obtain in real captures, since the scene and flare radiance are entangled at the sensor; separating them optically would require specialized capture hardware that is impractical for handheld video. We therefore evaluate decomposition against a model-derived reference, which we define and justify in Sec. 5.3 .
blocks.zh: 我们捕捉到9个不同场景,这些场景涵盖室内和室外环境、多种镜头类型(焦距和综艺),以及各种现实世界的光源 — — LED头灯、车间照明、智能手机闪光灯、街灯和紫色装饰灯 — — 以便引领广泛的反射耀斑模式。 我们捕捉到1⁄2分钟的序列,使用300300 — 400400平方英尺的视频帧进行训练,还有40幅来自剩余帧的图像进行测试。 这里远离训练轨迹的悬浮视线是不切实际的:只要耀斑仍然可见,我们只捕捉到每个序列,所以相机运动就被光线离开框和耀斑消失的点所包围,而不是偏好进行狭长的扫射. 因此,这些被搁置的框与训练框相互隔开,从而测试该范围内附近观点之间的插值;对新观点和场景的推断通过传输(第5.4节)和补充网页显示。 与普通场景内容不同,耀斑的外观受光线相对于光学轴的位置而不是场景点偏 Parlax的支配,而这种映射高度非线性:小相机或光运动可以在幽灵位置,光环范围,和螺旋方向上产生不成比例的较大变化(Sec. 5.5). 因此,将这种变形在附近框架之间插入是非三角性的。 与上面的5 5 - 场面清除数据集不同,每像素的地真耀斑图像和耀斑层在真实的捕捉中难以获得,因为场景和耀斑的光线缠绕在传感器上;在光学上将它们分离,需要专门的捕捉硬件,这对于手持视频是不切实际的. 因此,我们参照我们在第5.3节中界定和论证的模型参考来评估分解情况。

blocks.en: 5.1. Removing Lens Flares
blocks.zh: 5.1. 消除灯光

blocks.en: In this section, we evaluate the performance of our lens flare removal model. First, we compare our model against established baselines on the Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) benchmark for scattering flare removal. Then, we compare our model against baselines on our proposed VFX benchmark. One of the most significant benefits of our method is that it requires only 20 20 hours to fine-tune our model (on a single GPU), whereas our baselines take more than 4 4 days to train.
blocks.zh: 在这一节中,我们评价我们的镜头照明弹清除模型的性能. 首先,我们将我们的模型与Flare7K++的既定基线进行比较 (Dai等人,2023a)清除耀斑的基准。 然后,我们将我们的模型与我们提议的VFX基准的基线进行比较。 我们的方法最显著的好处之一是只需20个20小时就可以(在单一GPU上)微调我们的模型,而我们的基线则需要4天多的时间来训练.

blocks.en: 5.1.1. Scattering Flares
blocks.zh: 5.1.1. 扫射火焰

blocks.en: The Flare7K++ benchmark mainly evaluates scattering flare removal. We compare our model with the top-performing scattering-flare-removal models: Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) , FR ( Wu et al., 2021 ) , and ACL-FR ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) by retraining the models with our VFX dataset and procedural flares in addition to the Flare7K++ dataset. Further, we compare with the released versions of LightsOut ( Tsai et al., 2025 ) and FlareX ( Lishen et al., 2025 ) ; note that LightsOut is designed to outpaint off-screen light sources ahead of an existing removal network, whereas we evaluate it as a standalone remover. Quantitative results for the comparison are shown in Tab. 2 . As shown, our model, which incorporates supervision of light sources and lens glare, outperforms all existing models on the benchmark, which also contains lens glare. As shown in Fig. 10 , our models better recover the scene behind the flares and generate more plausible images. Furthermore, note that our model, trained without lens glares, also performs very well qualitatively in removing flares. Our baselines, however, still contain a substantial residual flare.

blocks.zh: 5.1.2. 反射火焰

blocks.en: Removing large reflective flares is particularly difficult, as most of the details that help a model recover the scene’s exact features are obscured by them. We train our models on our proposed flare-removal dataset. We show the quantitative results in Tab. 2 . We evaluate the models’ performance on 128 128 images of our proposed VFX benchmark. Ours outperforms all baselines on every metric, and Ours-wGlare on PSNR and LPIPS.

blocks.en: 5.1.3. Ablations

We evaluate our design choices of our flare removal model qualitatively in Fig. 11 , and quantitatively in Tab. 2 . One key design choice is to incorporate light sources into the supervision images, eliminating the need for a post-processing step to add light back to the flare-removed images, as in our baselines. We demonstrate this in ‘wo light’, where we train the model to remove light sources and then add them back as a post-processing step. While baseline models, especially Flare7K++ ( Dai et al., 2023a ) , perform well when a light source is added back to the images, we observed that our diffusion-based model does not perform as well on either benchmark (Tab. 2 , ‘wo light’).
Another important design choice is to fine-tune the VAE encoder with LoRA. We demonstrate the importance of this in ‘wo enc FT’, where we do not fine-tune the VAE encoder. Quantitatively, our models outperform the model without encoder finetuning. We believe this is due to the distribution of the flare-corrupted images not being close to the VAE’s training distribution. Finally, training without our VFX data specializes the model to scattering flares: it gains 0.28 0.28 dB on Flare7K++ ( 26.96 26.96 vs. 26.68 26.68 dB) but loses 1.16 1.16 dB on VFX ( 24.77 24.77 vs. 25.93 25.93 dB). While it still performs well at removing large reflective flares, it misses important flare regions and leaves flare artifacts, as shown in Fig. 11 .

blocks.en: 5.2. 3D Reconstruction with Flare Corruption
blocks.zh: 5.2. 3D 与火焰腐败一起重建

blocks.en: In this experiment, we demonstrate the performance of our model in removing flares consistently across multiple views. To achieve this, we train a 3DGS model on sequences captured with a light source and flare corruption in training views. We select approximately 10 % 10\% of the images for testing, ensuring they do not contain flares or light sources for a fair evaluation. We evaluate against ground-truth images ( not preprocessed by a flare-removal model).
blocks.zh: 在这个实验中,我们展示了我们的模型在从多种观点中一致清除耀斑方面的表现。 为了实现这一点,我们培训了一个3DGS模型,在训练视野中用光源捕获序列和耀斑腐败. 我们选择大约10%的图像进行测试,以确保它们不包含照明弹或光源,以便进行公正的评估。 我们对照地面真实图像(不是通过照明弹清除模型进行预处理)进行评估。

blocks.en: We train a 3DGS model on different sets of flare-removed images generated by our baseline flare-removal models. Quantitatively, 3DGS trained on our models’ outputs outperforms existing methods, as shown in Tab. 3 . These results are well substantiated qualitatively in Fig. 12 . It can be seen that inconsistent lens-flare removal across views by models leads to artifacts in reconstructions. It can also be seen that BilateralGrid ( Wang et al., 2024 ) fails to remove flares, as they are inherently different from image exposure changes across views. 3DGS trained on our flare-removed models yields far fewer artifacts, resulting in high-quality reconstructions.

blocks.en: 5.3. Flare Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 5.3. 火焰重建

blocks.en: We evaluate the performance of our flare representation model for reconstruction and decomposition. We compare these reconstructions with our baseline and ablation models.
blocks.zh: 我们评价我们用于重建和分解的耀斑代表模型的表现。 我们把这些重建与我们的基线和衰减模型相比较。

blocks.en: The target is not self-evident. A light source is a genuine scene emitter, yet the glare surrounding it is produced by the imaging system, so the boundary between ‘scene’ and ‘flare’ has to be stated rather than assumed. We settle it by choice of reference. Taking I removed I_{\text{removed}} , the output of our removal model Ours, as the flare-free reference, we require (i) the scene render to match I removed I_{\text{removed}} , and (ii) the flare branch’s contribution to match the residual I input − I removed I_{\text{input}}-I_{\text{removed}} . Because Ours retains the light source while removing the flare and the glare around it (Sec. 3.1 ), the emitter falls on the scene side and the artifacts it induces on the flare side. This reference measures the contribution of flares to the composite scene rather than the flare itself. We need this difference-based reference because rendering the flare Gaussians alone would composite them against an empty background, and we have no direct reference against which to evaluate such a render. We therefore compute the flare contribution as | I scene+flare − I scene | |I_{\text{scene+flare}}-I_{\text{scene}}| . Both sides of (ii) are thus formed alike, which makes the criterion agnostic to the compositing strategy.
blocks.zh: 目标并非不言而喻。 光源是真实的场景发射器,然而其周围的光线是由成像系统产生的,因此,必须说明 " 场景 " 和 " 火焰 " 之间的界限,而不是假设。 我们通过选择参考来解决这个问题。 我们要求 (一) 场景渲染来匹配我删除的 I_{\text{ removed} (二) 耀斑分支对剩余 I 输入的贡献 - 我删除了 I_{\text{ input{} - I_{\text{ removed} 。 因为Ours保留了光源,同时去除耀斑和周围的光辉(第3.1节),发射器掉在了现场一侧,它诱导的文物也掉在耀斑一侧. 这一参考衡量了照明弹对复合场景的贡献,而不是照明弹本身。 我们需要这种基于差异的提法,因为单凭高斯人一手就能把它们与空洞的背景结合起来,我们没有直接的提法来评价这种观点。 因此,我们计算耀斑贡献为: | I scene+flare — 我 scene_________________。 第(二)项的两面因此形成相同,这使得标准对堆肥策略不可知.

blocks.en: The residual in (ii) is not a pure flare layer. A flare saturates and occludes the scene behind it, so no exact flare is recoverable from a single image, and I input − I removed I_{\text{input}}-I_{\text{removed}} therefore also absorbs the discrepancy between the true occluded content and Ours’s reconstruction of it, including any light-source energy the removal model does not reproduce exactly. The flare branch is trained to account for whatever the removal model does not, so the two components together reconstruct the input regardless of where the removal model draws its boundary. Because flare Gaussians are composited in front of the scene, a transferred flare also carries its own light source into a new target (Fig. 1 ). It remains a close proxy for flare reconstruction quality, because reproducing the flare’s contribution to the composite is exactly what our flare branch is responsible for. As I removed I_{\text{removed}} is model-derived, the scene and flare metrics measure agreement with this reference rather than with an unobtainable ground truth: they are meaningful for comparing variants scored against a common reference, but not as absolute quality figures. Two facts limit this circularity: all metrics are computed at held-out frames that no model sees during training, and Ours was never trained on these scenes; it is validated separately on real paired captures (Flare7K++, Tab. 2 ) and, across views, by reconstructions that best match real flare-free captures (Sec. 5.2 ). What remains is shared bias: variants supervised with I removed I_{\text{removed}} inherit its systematic errors, which the reference also carries, so their scores are modestly favoured over variants that are not. Only the composite render is compared to the captured image directly, making it the sole removal-independent measure.

blocks.en:
The results in Fig. 13 demonstrate that 3DGS initialized with Colmap ( Schönberger et al., 2016 ; Schönberger and Frahm, 2016 ) can reconstruct some scattering flares close to the light source that are approximately 3D consistent, as Colmap provides some initialization for these flares. However, reflective flares in the given images are completely ignored, as they are highly variable in shape, color, and size across views, and Colmap cannot provide initializations for such 3D inconsistent objects. Our model, ‘Ours’, on the other hand, helps reconstruct the highly variable flare objects and represents them consistently across different views (see supplementary video for flares rendered from novel views).
On the composite Scene & Flare metric our model exceeds vanilla 3DGS by only 0.69 0.69 dB; this is expected, since both are fit to the same captured images and flare-affected pixels are a limited fraction of each frame, so even a model that smears or ignores the flare scores well on a whole-image metric. The two differ on decomposition (Tab. 4 , Fig. 13 ), where vanilla 3DGS produces no flare component at all and cannot be scored – whole-image metrics measure reconstruction quality rather than decomposition, so composite fidelity is a sanity check here, not the axis of comparison.

blocks.en: Our representation renders in real time at capture resolution. Flare Gaussians are emitted as standard 3DGS primitives and concatenated with the scene Gaussians for a single rasterization pass, so no additional render is required. Measured on an RTX 4090 at × 1080 1920\!\times\!1080 on a single-light scene ( hat ; 10,965 10{,}965 flare Gaussians alongside 162,283 162{,}283 scene Gaussians), the deformation pass takes 3.92 3.92 ms and the joint rasterization of all 173,248 173{,}248 Gaussians takes 6.86 6.86 ms, for a frame time of 10.79 10.79 ms ( 92.7 92.7 FPS). Rasterizing the scene alone – vanilla 3DGS on the same scene – takes 6.74 6.74 ms ( 148 148 FPS), so batching the flare Gaussians into the same pass adds only 1.8 % 1.8\% to rasterization cost; the deformation pass is the dominant expense of the flare model. It evaluates per Gaussian rather than per pixel, and we measure it to be independent of output resolution. We instantiate one flare model per light source, each with its own deformation network and canonical Gaussians, so this cost grows with the number of lights: 3.9 3.9 , 6.8 6.8 , and 11.1 11.1 ms for one, two, and three lights.

blocks.en: 5.3.1. Ablations

Our goals for the flare removal model are to decompose the input images to have a good 3D scene reconstruction alongside lens flares that can generalize to novel views. We perform ablations on our flare representation model to evaluate our design choices towards these goals. We show qualitative results in Fig. 13 , and quantitative results in Tab. 4 . In ‘Ours 2D’, we allow the flare Gaussians to move freely in the 2D plane, without our 1D representation. This model struggles to reconstruct flares since the Gaussians are unconstrained (flare PSNR 27.77 27.77 dB vs. 33.27 33.27 dB for Ours), and the composite reconstruction degrades correspondingly (Scene+Flare PSNR 27.76 27.76 dB, the lowest of all ablations). Next, we evaluate the effect of scene supervision on decomposition. In ‘Ours sup in-Flare’ and ‘Ours unsup’, we train the scene Gaussians with the reconstructed flare image subtracted from the input image and with no scene-only supervision, respectively. These models lead to inconsistent decompositions, missing different aspects of flares inconsistently across different scenes. However, ‘Ours unsup’, whose flare model augments 3DGS in reconstructing aspects of the captures that 3DGS misses, namely reflective lens flares, attains the highest composite PSNR of all variants. In ‘Ours wo δ l \delta_{l} ’, we train our model without the light position correction in Eq. ( 6 ). It performs on par with ‘Ours’, as the finer deformations δ f \delta_{f} absorb the light-position error (Sec. 5.5 ). Further, in ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’, we initialize the light source locations using the centroid of the scene’s Colmap point cloud with added noise, demonstrating that our model can fairly accurately reconstruct flares even without explicit light source detection, thanks to the light-position correction and finer deformations (Eq. ( 6 ), Eq. ( 5 )). In ‘Ours wo δ f \delta_{f} ’, where we train the model without the finer deformations δ f \delta_{f} (see Eq. ( 5 )), the model struggles to reconstruct asymmetric flares, leading to a slightly lower performance on flare reconstruction (PSNR of 32.99 32.99 dB). While the ‘Ours unsup’ achieves higher composite Scene+Flare PSNR ( 33.67 33.67 vs. 33.06 33.06 dB for Ours)—since the flare model’s additional capacity improves overall reconstruction—it performs poorly on scene decomposition ( 20.97 20.97 vs. 31.79 31.79 dB for Ours). Our model achieves the best flare decomposition (PSNR 33.27 33.27 dB) while remaining within 0.1 0.1 dB of the highest scene-decomposition PSNR ( 31.89 31.89 for ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’ vs. 31.79 31.79 dB for ‘Ours’). However, Ours outperforms ‘Ours wo G-SAM2’ in Flare decomposition reconstruction by ∼ 1.1 \sim 1.1 dB PSNR. Our model therefore offers the best scene/flare separation, which is the desired trade-off for our decomposable-reconstruction goal.

blocks.en: The ablations above are not only design controls; each also corresponds to a useful operating point of our framework. The default Ours setting bundles the light source and its flare into a single, self-contained 3D flare effect, suitable for transferring the captured flare to other scenes (e.g., VFX). Ours unsup instead prioritizes faithful composite reconstruction with flares, giving the highest Scene+Flare PSNR ( 33.67 33.67 , vs. 33.06 33.06 dB for the default), and serves applications that need flare-preserving re-rendering. The user can thus pick the training configuration matching the downstream task.

blocks.en:
We first demonstrate transfer onto a
target that has no associated 3D reconstruction at all: an arbitrary 2D target
image (Fig. 1 ). Because such a target carries no camera pose,
scene geometry, or light-source depth, the camera- and light-conditioned
anchoring used for scene transfer (below) does not apply. Instead, we specify a
single 2D point in the target image as the desired light-source location –
either manually or via the same Grounded-SAM2 detection used elsewhere in our
pipeline – and query the flare MLP with the source camera and source light as
before, so the transferred flare keeps its learned in-distribution shape and
color, while its placement is now driven by this target-image point rather than
a projected 3D light position. The resulting flare Gaussians are rendered and
alpha-composited directly onto the target image. As the target image carries no
depth information, we do not perform a visibility test in this setting: the
flare is composited unconditionally on top of the target image.

To demonstrate that our learned flares are not tied to the scene they were
optimized on, we transfer flares trained on three source scenes – two
from our captured reconstruction dataset (Sec. 5.3 ) and
one additional captured scene not part of either dataset (also used for source
flares in Fig. 1 ) – onto a single target scene that
likewise does not appear in either of our captured datasets
(Sec. 4 ) and is used only as a transfer target
(Fig. 14 ). Both of these additional captures use the sun
as the light source, diversifying beyond the light types in
Sec. 5.3 . Each flare MLP
ensemble is optimized jointly with its source scene’s Gaussians and is
conditioned on the source cameras and light positions. At transfer time we
decouple appearance from placement . The MLP is conditioned on camera
and light positions and can be queried at any of them, as the supplementary video shows
by sweeping the light along the principal-point line and then moving the camera as well.
For transfer, however, we deliberately query it with the source camera and the source light it was trained with, since a target
camera may lie well outside the source capture’s distribution and would elicit an
extrapolated flare. This keeps the learned flare shape and color in-distribution, while
the resulting flare Gaussians are anchored to the target scene by placing them relative
to the target camera and aiming them at the target scene’s light position(s). For each frame we first
rasterize the target Gaussians from the target camera, which also yields an
inverse-depth map used for a per-light visibility test: a flare is instantiated
only for target lights that are not occluded by target geometry. One flare is
built per visible target light and the instances are merged, then composited
with the target render so that the transferred flare correctly blends with (and
is occluded by) the target scene. Because the flare follows the target cameras,
we render along the target scene’s smooth video trajectory to produce the
transfer sequences. Since the flare is represented explicitly as Gaussians, it
also remains directly editable after transfer: the bottom row of
Fig. 14 shows a transferred flare with its Gaussians
uniformly scaled by 2 × 2\times , giving simple artistic control over the flare’s

blocks.en: 6. Future Work
blocks.zh: 6个 未来工作

blocks.en: Our flare representation model improves 3DGS’s performance in scenes with lens flares by decomposing the scene into a lens-flare component and a flare-free component, enabling many downstream applications such as flare transfer and editing. While our 2D removal model already handles ring-shaped flares (we explicitly include procedurally generated rings in its training set, see Sec. 4 ), their 3D representation remains an open problem: because our flare Gaussians have peak opacity at the mean and decrease radially away from it (see Fig. 17 ), a single Gaussian cannot form the annular profile required for rings. We therefore leave the 3D representation of ring-shaped flares for future work. Further, light sources out of frame are handled based on projected depth, however, those occluded by scene geometry within a captured view are currently handled implicitly through our flare representation model, rather than through an explicit occlusion-aware mechanism; we leave this to future work.
blocks.zh: 我们的耀斑表示模型通过将场景分解成透镜荧光元件和无耀斑元件,改进了3DGS在场景中的性能,使耀斑传递和编辑等许多下游应用得以实现. 虽然我们的2D清除模型已经处理环形耀斑(我们明确在其训练集中包括程序生成的环,参见 Sec. 4 ),但其3D的表达方式仍是一个公开的问题:因为我们的耀斑高斯人在平均值上有峰值不透明度,并且从中辐射减少(参见图 17),单个高斯人无法形成环所需的废止配置. 因此,我们将环形照明弹的3D表示留给今后的工作。 此外,超出框架的光源是根据预测的深度处理的,但是,目前通过我们的耀斑表示模式,而不是通过明确的隐蔽-意识机制,暗中处理在所捕捉的视野内被场景几何所占据的光源;我们将此留给今后的工作处理。

blocks.en: Moreover, our flare removal model is bounded by the flare types represented in our training datasets (Sec. 4 ); flares that fall far outside this distribution are harder for it to remove convincingly. Additionally, since a real scene cannot be captured simultaneously with and without the same flare, the removal model is trained on flares composited onto otherwise clean images rather than on paired real captures; closing this synthetic-to-real gap would likely require a capture rig that optically isolates the flare, which we leave to future work.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们的照明弹清除模型以我们训练数据集(第4节)中的照明弹类型为界;远离这种分布的照明弹更难令人信服地清除。 此外,由于一个真实的场景不能与同一照明弹同时捕获,而且没有同样的照明弹,因此清除模型被训练用于将复合到其他干净的图像上的照明弹,而不是成对的真正捕获;要缩小这一合成-实际差距,很可能需要一种将照明弹光学隔离的捕获装置,我们留给未来工作。

blocks.en: 7. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7. 结论

blocks.en: We introduced two models: a lens-flare removal model and, to our knowledge, the first lens-flare representation reconstructed from captured multi-view images. We compiled a dataset of full-image lens flares from publicly available real-world data. Further, we evaluated our flare removal models on the established Flare7k++ benchmark and our proposed VFX benchmark, where on each one of our two models outperforms all compared baselines. Moreover, our 2D flare removal model outperforms baselines, even in 3D scenes, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on our proposed benchmark for consistent flare removal across multiple views. We used flare removal to develop the lens-flare representation model and demonstrated a decomposed reconstruction of a given scene with flares into scene Gaussians and our flare Gaussians. We believe these models would be useful for different downstream tasks and end-user applications.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了两种模型:一种镜头-荧幕清除模型,据我们所知,第一个镜头-荧幕代表从捕获的多视图图像中重建. 我们从公开的真人世界数据中 汇编了一套全图像透镜照明弹 此外,我们还根据既定的Flare7k++基准和我们提议的VFX基准评估了我们的耀斑清除模型,在这两个模型中,每个模型的绩效都超过了所有比较基线。 此外,我们的2D照明弹清除模型甚至超过了基线,在三维场景中也是如此,它显示了我们提出的在多种观点中一致清除照明弹的基准的最新性能。 我们利用照明弹的清除来开发透镜-喷射的表示模型,并演示了特定场景的分解重建,将照明弹制成高斯人和我们的照明弹. 我们认为,这些模型将有益于不同的下游任务和最终用户应用。

Retain original colors”. We train the model with a batch size of 1 1 for 200 ​ k 200k iterations with a learning rate of 1 ​ e − 4 1e^{-4} on an Nvidia A100 GPU, which takes approximately 20 20 hours; training only ≈ 2 % {\approx}2\% of the model is the main reason it converges so much faster than the baselines, which are trained from scratch and require more than four days. blocks.en: A.1.2. Flare representation
blocks.zh: A.1.2. 公开代表

blocks.en: For each light source, the deformation network is an instant-NGP-style model: the light input (the absolute normalized image-plane offset of the projected light from the principal point, together with its norm) and the camera position are encoded with multiresolution hash grids of 16 16 levels and 2 2 features per level, a base resolution of 16 16 , hash-table sizes of 2 17 2^{17} and 2 15 2^{15} , and per-level scales of 1.8 1.8 and 1.6 1.6 , respectively; the 1D canonical position uses a frequency encoding with 3 3 bands. The result is decoded by an MLP backbone with 3 3 hidden layers of width 128 128 and ReLU activations. Flare Gaussians are placed at a depth of 0.21 0.21 in the camera frame, just beyond the near plane. We optimize the network and encodings with Adam at a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} . The canonical flare Gaussians use a position learning rate of 1.6 × 10 − 4 1.6\times 10^{-4} , decayed exponentially to 1.6 × 10 − 6 1.6\times 10^{-6} , and learning rates of 2.5 × 10 − 3 2.5\times 10^{-3} , 0.05 0.05 , 0.1 0.1 and 10 − 3 10^{-3} for their features, opacities, scales and rotations, respectively. We train for 30,000 30{,}000 iterations. We initialize 200 200 flare Gaussians at different positions along a line with reasonable sizes, ensuring that they do not occupy the entire image. We clone and prune the flare Gaussians every 500 500 iterations, from 1 ​ k 1k to 12 ​ k 12k iterations. We allow cloning to be aggressive for all opacities above 0.005 0.005 , with a clone ratio of 0.2 0.2 , and perturb cloned Gaussians with Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.02 0.02 . We compare the union of predicted SAM2 masks against the ground-truth masks at
the pixel level (precision, recall, F1, IoU), sweeping GroundingDINO’s
box-confidence threshold from 0.05 0.05 to 0.80 0.80 ( Fig. 19 ), since
this threshold alone governs the pipeline’s precision–recall trade-off (SAM2 only segments the boxes it is given). The raw pipeline peaks at F1 0.31 0.31 (threshold 0.50 0.50 ): low thresholds yield many spurious boxes, and SAM2 tends to
segment the illuminated halo rather than the compact source. Our refinements –
resolving overlapping boxes and discarding non-over-exposed detections –
substantially improve precision over the raw pipeline, at a small cost in recall at the lowest thresholds, reaching F1 0.66 0.66 (precision 0.51 0.51 , recall 0.93 0.93 , IoU 0.49 0.49 ) at threshold 0.20 0.20 (Fig. 20 ).

NMS, motivating our containment-based criterion instead. Lowering the threshold
to 0.10 0.10 inflates proposals roughly tenfold, of which the refinements prune only ∼ 82 % \sim\!82\% . Detection is also intermittent across frames ( 2,216 2{,}216 frames with
no detection, 319 319 fully filtered), which is precisely what our multi-view 3D
aggregation with TRASE ( Li et al., 2026 ) resolves, consolidating noisy per-frame
2D detections into a consistent set of 3D light sources per scene.
